title.analysis: Authentic title "Track These 4 Numbers To Retire Decades Early" is a numbered-checklist promise. The script delivers four numbers (savings rate, annual spending, real return, multiple) through three composites, and is unusually candid that a 50-year horizon raises the target and that many early retirements are involuntary.

script.stored_text_completeness: All 18187 canonical characters read sequentially in full in 1 bounded ranges; auto-generated untimed text; stored text ends on the community call ("...come tell me in our school community when it moves.") with no separate sign-off; composites rendered as Jaimie/Jamie, Jade and Grace; a missing full stop after "under 20" and "end of 2025"; audio, timed delivery and editing unverified.
script.opening_words: Somewhere out there is someone taking home the same paycheck you are. Same city, same zero in the same account the year you both turned 29. One of you stops working 13 years before the other, and nothing in your bank app will ever tell you which of you it is. Her name is Jaimie. 3 years in, she got a raise, moved somewhere the dishwasher worked, financed a car that still smelled new, and stopped checking the grocery total,
script.ending_words: you have, how much time. Jade owned 22 years by the time Jaimie owned 10, and he never once out-earned her. She had more money, he had more life. Whatever your number is, it's either going up or it isn't, and it does not care even slightly how your year is going. Go find out which one you're on, and come tell me in our school community when it moves.
script.analysis: Full 18187 canonical characters read. A single-narrator explainer with composites Jaimie, Jade and Grace: hook on who stops working first, savings rate and the income-blind table, annual spending and lifestyle creep, the $300-per-$1 rule, the ACA subsidy cliff, real return (fees, cash timing, valuations), the multiple, safe withdrawal rates for long horizons, early-access doors (rule of 55, 72(t), Roth ladder), the crossover point, Jaimie's layoff, EBRI forced-retirement data, a community promotion and disclaimer, and a close. Arithmetic reproduces throughout; the savings-rate statistic and composite gaps are unverified.
beat_map: Hook: three people, one finish line.
Number two: spending and Jaimie's raise.
Number three: real return and Grace's fees.
